About Invisible

Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most.

Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere.

Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets.

Profitable for more than half a decade, Invisible reached $134M in revenue and ranked as the number two fastest growing AI company on the 2024 Inc. 5000. In September 2025, we raised $100M in growth capital to accelerate our mission of making AI actually work in the enterprise and to advance our platform technology.

About the Role

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to set the technical strategy for Data Labs, the team that builds the benchmarking systems, data pipelines, and RL environments behind our AI training engagements. The frontier labs and enterprises we work with are changing how they train, evaluate, and deploy models every quarter. Your job is to see where that market is going and make sure Data Labs is built for it before our clients ask.

You'll decide which capabilities we invest in, which we standardize into platform, and which we leave to individual engagements. You'll track how training methods, evaluation practices, and data needs are shifting across the industry, and turn that into a technical roadmap and a point of view our commercial and research teams can sell against.

You'll lead a group of engineering managers, forward deployed engineers (FDEs), and senior ICs, and partner closely with applied research, product, and go-to-market leadership. This is a hands-on strategic role. You won't spend much time writing code, but you'll stay close enough to the technical work to make and defend hard architectural calls, and close enough to clients to know which calls matter.

What You'll Do

Technical Strategy & Roadmap
- Own the multi-year technical strategy for Data Labs, and translate it into a roadmap tied to where the AI training and evaluation market is heading.
- Decide where to build shared platform versus engagement-specific solutions, weighing reuse against team autonomy so platforms speed teams up rather than creating over-dependency.
- Set architectural direction for benchmarking infrastructure, data pipelines, and RL environments so they stay reproducible, portable across client deployments, and ready for the next generation of training methods.
- Anticipate technical shifts 6–18 months out, such as new post-training techniques, agentic evaluation, and synthetic data, and place the bets that keep Invisible ahead of them.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. Ursa Major is seeking an executive technology leader to serve as our Chief Information Security Officer (CISO w/ clearance) . Reporting to the executive leadership team, the CISO will establish enterprise-wide information security ownership across our multi-site engineering, manufacturing, and test facilities. Working in direct, strategic lockstep with our Facility Security Officer (FSO), who leads personnel clearances, physical security, and overall NISPOM facility compliance, the CISO serves as the ultimate authority for digital, technical, and operational cybersecurity.

We are not looking for an administrator who leads from behind a desk or relies on enterprise bureaucracy. We need a builder who leads from the front—an executive with deep roots in Aerospace & Defense (A&D) who knows what mature security infrastructure looks like and possesses the hands-on drive to build, scale, and mature our systems from the ground up.

Sitting at the intersection of defense compliance, manufacturing velocity, and enterprise IT, you will own the overarching risk management strategy for both unclassified and classified programs. You will champion our hybrid CMMC Level 2 enclave expansion, govern the technical architecture of classified defense enclaves (Secret / SAP), protect critical Intellectual Property, and establish the cyber risk governance required for a high-growth defense firm preparing for public-company operations.

Responsibilities:
- Define and execute Ursa Major’s enterprise cybersecurity and information assurance strategy across all corporate, manufacturing, engineering, and classified program environments.
- Lead from the front to build, mentor, and inspire a world-class cybersecurity engineering and compliance team, fostering a culture of operational enablement, technical rigor, and deep cross-functional partnership.
- Direct the continuous advancement and accreditation of our CMMC Level 2 / NIST SP 800-171 architecture, ensuring Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and defense technical data flow securely across multi-site operations without impeding engineering velocity.

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.


🛠️ About our Teams


At Wayve, we are building AI that learns to drive from experience.

We do not hand-code cars to drive. Our models learn from data gathered across the real world, making our ability to identify, understand and learn from the right data fundamental to everything we build.

Our Data organisation sits at the heart of this learning loop. It works across AI, Science, Validation, Product, Compute and our commercial programmes to determine what data Wayve needs, how we acquire and understand it, and how we turn it into measurable improvements in our AI Driver.

The scale and shape of the problem is unique. Our data comes from our own vehicles, OEM programmes, partners and external sources, spanning different vehicles, sensors, markets and driving environments. Within that corpus, the most valuable examples are often the hardest to find: rare behaviours, unusual interactions, safety-critical events and the long tail of real-world driving.

We are looking for a VP of Data to lead this organisation and own the data strategy behind Wayve’s autonomous driving technology.

🧠 Your day-to-day


As VP of Data, you will have end-to-end ownership of how Wayve uses data to improve our AI.

You will set the strategy across the complete AI learning cycle, determining what data we need and how it should drive model performance, from foundation model training through specialised driving capabilities and production programmes.

You will lead a multidisciplinary Data organisation and work closely with senior leaders across Engineering, AI, Science, Validation, Product, Compute, Finance and Commercial teams.

This is not simply about building systems that process data. You will be responsible for deciding what data matters and why, making significant technical and investment decisions, and building the strategy, organisation and learning loop that enables Wayve to learn from the real world faster.

The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

The journey to space starts with the engines.

We design, build, and deploy advanced propulsion systems that power national security missions, hypersonic capabilities, and the future of space access.

Our mission requires an extraordinary team—one that will mold tomorrow’s critical technologies while deploying today’s best. We are an intrinsically motivated team with a passion for solving complex technical problems and empowering each other every day, knowing that there is always room for growth.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the Head of Digital Operations, the Director of Enterprise Systems & Software (ESS) is a strategic executive technology leader responsible for establishing central ownership, governance, and architectural rigor across Ursa Major's entire internal enterprise digital landscape.

This role officially transitions core enterprise system ownership out of legacy, ad-hoc structures (previously managed under Digital Manufacturing) and establishes a dedicated department built on extreme system ownership. You will lead a high-performing team of dedicated Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across core enterprise platforms (PLM, ERP, MES, Data/BI) alongside our internal Software Engineering organization (which builds custom internal web applications, including our engine testing solution and enterprise integration middleware). Day 1 leadership scope includes inheriting an established team (1x Product Owner, 2x Senior Software Developers, and a Manager of Digital Manufacturing transitioning to lead Enterprise Systems Integrations) alongside hiring dedicated Systems Engineers/Architects across PLM (Windchill), ERP (Odoo), MES (Critical Manufacturing), Atlassian, and Data Science/Analytics.

As Ursa Major scales from 380 to 500+ employees and prepares for public-company operations, you will lead the evolution of our ERP (Odoo) into a public-company-ready platform. Over time, your organization will systematically absorb and professionalize adjacent business-critical systems—such as HighQA, Jama, Ignition, and Atlassian—building an integrated digital thread across ISA-95 levels and laying the technical foundation for a fully operational Digital Twin across our manufacturing facilities by EOY 2027.

Responsibilities:
- Establish centralized ownership and serve as the executive authority for all business-critical enterprise platforms, enforcing to internal stakeholders that ESS provides dedicated SME ownership, administration, and support.

Everything the Forward Deployed team learns working at the edge with our customers is fed back to our platform teams to improve Hadrian’s product for all customers.

### **About Pedestal Health**

  

Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE) is a rapidly growing company at the intersection of clinical research, healthcare, and technology, focused on reimagining clinical evidence generation. The company partners with pharmaceutical and biotech companies, providers, and payers to generate rigorous, multimodal evidence that supports clinical, regulatory, and strategic decision-making across the full lifecycle of care. Pedestal Health is committed to advancing medical decision-making to improve patient outcomes. Pedestal Health is a Highlander Health company. Learn more at pedestalhealth.com.

### **The Role**

Every clinical data point has a life story. A clinician records it during a visit, and it passes through many systems and hands before reaching a regulatory submission. Multiply that by dozens of health systems, each handling data differently, then add claims, trial forms, and other data feeds. Add the fact that 80-90% of healthcare data lives in unstructured formats, and the result is a mosaic. This mosaic is only as trustworthy as the way its pieces fit together. As trials and real-world data blend into continuous evidence generation, this mosaic is becoming the field's central problem.

Pedestal Health is hiring a Head of Technology to build the foundation that makes the mosaic trustworthy. That means a documented chain of custody from the point of care to the final dataset, a single quality standard across every source, the ability to extract valuable information from unstructured data, and the security that earns the trust of health systems and sponsors. In this role, you will own two areas that depend on each other. The first is the data engineering, platforms, and user-facing applications that turn clinical data from our health system partners into products our clients rely on. The second is the IT and security programs that keep our people productive, our systems protected, and our partners confident in how we handle their data. The right candidate will have experience working with health systems and healthcare data, preferably electronic health record (EHR) data.

We are EnduroSat! A fast-growing space scale-up at the forefront of satellite innovation, specializing in advanced software-flexible satellites for commercial, governmental, and scientific endeavors.

* **This is more than a job, it's a mission**

  We are making space universally accessible and redefining the possible
* **We get things done**

  We take ownership of what we do and we work hard to make a difference

**What is the role?**

As our VP of Engineering & Chief Engineer, you will own the final technical delivery of EnduroSat US across hundreds of missions and the engineering organization that creates it. Systems engineering, mechanical, structural and FEA, thermal, software, and the other disciplines all report to you. You hold final technical authority on US programs: you decide what the system looks like, you sign off on the final architecture, and you are accountable when it does not work.  
  
The engineering problem here is not clean-sheet design. Our satellites share a common platform, and the value we deliver is the last mile on top of it — the integration, and mission-specific design that turns a proven bus into a spacecraft that does a particular customer's job. You will assess whether our existing system design can meet a given mission, decide where it must change, and conceive adapted or new capability where it cannot. That takes deeper judgment than drawing from scratch, because every decision must survive contact with a platform, a schedule, and a supply chain that already exist.  
  
You will be in front of customers regularly — large commercial, civil, and defense organizations whose engineering teams will test whether our answers hold up. You will shape mission concepts during capture, defend architectures at PDR and CDR, and make requirements less dumb. You need the depth to take final decisions yourself and exceptional focus to ignore the noise so a mission can achieve what it needs on time and on budget, not the perfect solution that never comes.  
  
You will work as a peer to our VP of Mission & Programs, who owns delivery and the program relationship. You own what we build and whether it will work; they own getting it delivered and flown. You will also be in close contact with the European technological leadership who own the platform you are building on — keeping US and European engineering aligned on standards, architecture, and interfaces is part of this job, not an afterthought.  
This role is based in Los Angeles and is primarily on-site, with travel to customers and to our European headquarters. You will report to C-level management.

The Role
As Director of Data Science & Analytics, you will build and lead the team that turns Coherent's manufacturing, supply chain, and commercial data into better decisions. You will set the analytics strategy, deliver production machine learning, and partner with operations, engineering, finance, and sales leaders. Your work will directly improve yield, capacity planning, cost, and speed to market as we scale output for AI infrastructure customers.
What You'll Do
- Set the strategy. Define and run Coherent's data science and analytics roadmap. Tie every initiative to business goals and track its measurable return.
- Deliver models that ship. Lead the development and deployment of predictive models, machine learning, and statistical analysis. Priority areas include yield and process optimization, predictive maintenance, demand forecasting, and supply chain planning.
- Build and lead the team. Hire, develop, and manage data scientists, analysts, and ML and data engineers. Create a culture of rigor, ownership, and collaboration.
- Own the platform. Guide the data and ML infrastructure, including cloud data platforms, pipelines, MLOps, and BI tools. Make sure it scales across global fabs and sites.
- Drive business impact. Turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for executives. Partner with operations, engineering, product, finance, and sales to put solutions into daily use.
- Establish governance. Set data quality, governance, and model-risk standards. Ensure compliance with security, privacy, and export-control requirements.
- Bring in what's next. Evaluate emerging methods, including generative AI and LLMs. Pilot the ones that prove value and scale them.

What You Bring
- Bachelor's degree in statistics, computer science, mathematics, engineering, economics, or a related field.
- 10+ years in data science or analytics, including 5+ years leading teams of data scientists, analysts, or engineers.
- Hands-on expertise in Python and SQL, plus machine learning, statistical modeling, and experimental design.
- A track record of taking models from prototype to production and measuring their business value.
- Experience with modern data and ML platforms, such as Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, or AWS, Azure, or GCP services.
- Clear, concise communication with executives and non-technical partners.
- The ability to rank competing priorities by business impact and say no to the rest.
Nice to Have
- Master's or PhD in a quantitative field.
- Experience in semiconductor, photonics, optical networking, or other high-tech manufacturing.
- Familiarity with manufacturing data, such as MES, SPC, test and yield data, or equipment sensor data.
- Experience deploying generative AI or LLM solutions in an enterprise setting.
- Certifications such as AWS Machine Learning, Databricks, PMP, or CIPP.

Safety Requirements
All employees are required to follow the site EHS procedures and Coherent Corp. Corporate EHS standards.

Fervo Energy (NASDAQ: FRVO) is a modern power company developing next-generation geothermal resources to meet the growing demand for affordable, reliable, 24/7 carbon-free energy. Our mission is to transform geothermal into America’s most dependable and affordable source of clean, around-the-clock power. By combining innovations in horizontal drilling, fiber-optic sensing, and advanced reservoir engineering, Fervo has developed a repeatable approach to building utility-scale enhanced geothermal systems. Our flagship Cape Station development in Utah is planned to deliver 500 MW of firm, carbon-free power, and we are advancing a development pipeline of more than 50 GW. Join us and work alongside world-class engineers, geoscientists, operators, project builders, and business leaders working to make geothermal a cornerstone of a more reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy future.

The Director of Threat Exposure & Assurance Management is a senior technology leader within centralized IT who has built, delivered or operated enterprise services. Enterprise Cybersecurity owns policy, standards and threat intelligence; this role owns the speed and consistency of CITO execution and measurable risk reduction. Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

Everything the Forward Deployed team learns working at the edge with our customers is fed back to our platform teams to improve Hadrian’s product for all customers.

Recent projects have included standing up Factories-as-a-Service for the Armed Forces and multiple primes, extending Opus into new manufacturing domains such as energetics, and taking a product that was built for a single program into a $B+ product line.

About Helion

We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone.

Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion.

This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait.

Every Helion fusion pulse runs current through semiconductor switches operated well beyond commercial ratings. Our next generation of fusion machines requires devices designed for our circuits rather than adapted to them, gated devices integrated as multi-die modules, and packaging that survives repetitive high-energy pulsing for power plant-scale lifetimes. You will lead the team that delivers these, from device physics through a development-scale fabrication capability to pilot module assembly and test, and you will carry it into high-volume production with external fabrication partners. Your team’s work will help determine how reliably Helion’s power plants operate, how frequently they can pulse, and how effectively we can manufacture and deploy future plants.

The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards.  Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day.  We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Who We Are:

We build the intelligence that lets robots sense, reason, and act in the real world, moving beyond the lab and into everyday industrial settings like warehouses and factories. Our technology closes the automation gaps that traditional systems can't solve. We are on a mission to redefine how physical work gets done, and we're looking for curious, bold thinkers to help shape the future of robotics with us.

Overview:

Our AI-driven pick-and-place and returns-handling cells combine robot arms, adaptive force-controlled grippers, AI vision and a safety cabinet, all driven by Cortex, our vision-language-action model. They run in live warehouse and logistics operations across the EU and US, and our deployed fleet is growing from around 50 cells to several hundred. Customer uptime now needs a dedicated owner. We're looking for a Director of Technical Support to build our customer-facing support function, covering everything from a customer opening a ticket to a cell back at target uptime. This is a player-coach role: you will stay hands-on technically while you hire the team and put the systems in place. You will work closely with our Hardware Product Engineering and Supply Chain leads.

Your Responsibilities:

Support Desk & Remote Diagnostics

 - Stand up the support desk, including ticket intake, triage, severity tiers, response and restore targets and an SLA framework

 - Define a coverage model for the EU and a plan for US time zones as the fleet grows

 - Build remote diagnostics on top of Cortex telemetry so most issues are triaged and fixed without a site visit

Escalation & Field Service

 - Run a closed escalation loop with Engineering, so field failures are triaged, root-caused and fixed in the product

 - Coordinate field service, including dispatch, on-site playbooks and third-party field technicians where needed

 - Identify the top recurring field failures and get them onto the product roadmap

Spares, RMA & Customer Enablement

 - Own the customer-facing RMA process and spare parts availability at customer sites, working with Supply Chain on procurement and logistics

 - Build customer onboarding, operator training, documentation and a knowledge base so customers can handle routine issues themselves

Metrics & Team

 - Own fleet uptime, MTTR, first-contact and first-visit resolution, SLA attainment and CSAT, and drive them up as the fleet grows

 - Hire and lead the first support and field engineers

 - Take front-line support duty off the founders and wider team

Qualifications:

Education and Experience

 - 8+ years in technical support, field service or after-sales for complex hardware, including several years leading teams

 - A track record of building a technical support, field service or after-sales function from scratch for a deployed hardware product as the installed base grew from tens to hundreds of sites

 - Hands-on experience setting up remote diagnostics and telemetry, ticketing and SLAs, escalation to enginee

As **Director, Distribution & Logistics Analytics & Decision Intelligence**, you will lead the global strategy, roadmap, and delivery of analytics, decision intelligence, and AI-enabled solutions across our Distribution & Logistics (D&L) network. You will transform operational challenges into scalable data products, insights, predictive analytics, and decision-support capabilities that improve service, cost, efficiency, resilience, and sustainability.

As the senior business product leader for D&L analytics, you will partner with Global and Regional D&L leaders, Supply Chain Planning & Analytics, Product, Engineering, and Data & Analytics teams to define analytics priorities, standardize KPIs, shape data products and semantic-layer capabilities, and accelerate adoption of AI-driven decision-making solutions.

This role reports to the **VP, Supply Chain Planning & Analytics**.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Own the global D&L Analytics & Decision Intelligence roadmap, prioritizing opportunities based on business impact, scalability, and user needs.
* Serve as the strategic analytics partner to global and regional Distribution & Logistics leaders, translating operational challenges into actionable insights and technology-enabled solutions.

  + Supply chain sustainability
  + Carrier and 3PL performance
  + Distribution center operations
  + Outbound transportation and omnichannel fulfillment
* Define and govern enterprise D&L KPIs, metrics, and business definitions to drive global consistency and transparency.

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. You will set direction for the team, support individual growth, and make sure the group can respond effectively to both immediate operational issues and longer term reliability challenges.

Bevi is on a mission to transform how beverages are delivered and consumed. Our connected beverage platform eliminates the need for single-use bottles and cans, making it easy, fun, and sustainable to stay hydrated. As the category leader in IoT-enabled beverage technology, we're building a future where Bevi machines are everywhere people live, work, and connect. We've raised over $160M in venture capital, serve thousands of customers across the US, Canada, UK and Ireland, and we've been rapidly growing year over year, saving over 1 billion bottles from waste. In addition to driving hypergrowth with our current product line, Bevi is heavily investing in new product development.

We are hiring a Director of Program Management to lead Bevi's central PMO. The PMO runs our new product introduction (NPI) programs from concept to launch. The team includes five program managers and sits in Operations, reporting to the COO.

This is a leadership role and a hands-on one. You will lead and develop the team, set the standard for how Bevi runs hardware programs, and run one of our most important NPI programs yourself. Our goal is to reduce our NPI cycle time with a higher predictability and quality. This role is central to getting there.

Your Day to Day

Lead the PMO
- Lead, coach and grow a team of program managers running complex, cross-functional hardware programs.
- Set the standard for how Bevi runs NPI programs and hold the team to it.
- Own Bevi's phase gate process. Each gate ends in a clear go, no-go or recycle decision, and open items carry forward with owners.

Run programs well
- Lead by example, taking on NPI programs directly as needed while building the team.
- Make sure every program has an aggressive, credible schedule that the team believes in and that is updated every week.
- Name risks early, assign owners and track the inputs that drive them: drawings, test results, open decisions and supplier dates.
- Base status on evidence (test data, released drawings, placed POs), not verbal updates. Raise issues before dates are missed, with options.
- Get the right people in the room to make decisions, and log them.
- Report program status to the leadership team and the Board.

Work across the company
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Service and Sales so programs launch at target quality, cost and supply readiness.
- Work with the leadership team and Product on portfolio priorities. Make resource and schedule tradeoffs visible so they can decide.
- Manage programs that involve contract manufacturers and design partners, including partners in Asia.

Make the PMO more efficient
- Keep core teams small and meetings focused on decisions and issues.
- Move program information to one system of record, so status is updated once and every report pulls from it.
- Use automation and AI to cut the time PMs spend compiling updates.
- Run post-program reviews and use what we learn to improve the playbook.

This is both a leadership role and a builder role. You manage the team and you own the outcomes.

- Own the Finance Capability & Technology, FP&A/Commercial pillar end-to-end — roadmap, delivery, operating model, and stakeholder governance across FP&A, Commercial Finance, and Sales Finance intelligence domains
- Lead and develop three Finance AI Leads and two Managers across Chicago, Amsterdam, and Mexico GCC — set priorities, run structured reviews, build technical and commercial depth, and hold the bar on output quality across a globally distributed team

About Jetson

Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

The Opportunity:

A heat pump is a fifteen-year relationship with a homeowner, and the second year matters as much as the first week. This role owns whether Jetson's systems keep working — and how fast we respond when they don't.

As Director of Technical Service, you lead Jetson's service organization and act as the company's senior technical authority in the field. You own callback rate, first-time fix rate, and time to resolution. You own warranty administration and the money we recover from manufacturers, customers and CARE programs. And because service data is the most honest feedback loop in the business, you own pushing what breaks in the field back into equipment selection, install standards, commissioning requirements, and crew training. This is a build-and-run role: you'll be designing the service function while operating it, across multiple markets at once.

What You'll Do:
- Lead and develop the technical service organization, including system designers and technical support staff; define coverage model, role scorecards, and the hiring plan as the installed base grows
- Own callback rate, first-time fix rate, and time to resolution on service calls, and set service level expectations by issue severity
- Build the remote triage and diagnostic function so issues are resolved without a truck roll wherever possible
- Own service capacity, dispatch, and on-call coverage, including surge planning for heating and cooling season peaks
- Own warranty administration and manufacturer claims, and recover cost wherever warranty applies
- Feed field failure data back into equipment selection, system design, install standards, and training, and hold those loops closed
- Partner with Director of Customer Success and Director of Production Coordination  on service recovery, escalation handling, and customer communication during outages
- Partner with Supply Chain on service parts strategy, truck stock, and warranty inventory
- Serve as final technical escalation authority, including safety, code compliance, and refrigerant handling issues
- Report weekly to leadership on callbacks, first-time fix, open service aging, and warranty recovery, with root cause and a plan attached to each

What You Bring:

This job combines two things that usually sit with different people: owning products and building them. One product is a real-time tracking and communications app that hundreds of thousands of families and their school districts rely on, where a wrong notification reaches a parent waiting at a bus stop. The other is the technology behind a service for students with special transportation needs, students experiencing homelessness, and out-of-district students, delivered through contracted local transportation providers.
Each product has a Business Product Owner who owns its business outcomes, priorities, and commercial decisions. You are their partner on the IT side, owning how those priorities become software within the lines our product management operating model sets. It gets built in an agentic delivery framework owned by a senior technical team. You own its product side: the specs, acceptance criteria, and evals that go in, and the call on whether the result met the business need.
You also build. In traditional product management, requirements get written, handed to engineering, and interpreted somewhere along the way. Here, a conversation with a stakeholder can become working software in days, and the person who had the conversation is often the one directing the agents that build it. You should already be building with agents, even if it is not yet how you do all of your work. In this role, building stops being something you do alongside product management and becomes how you do it.
You will start with a small team, so expect to lead and build at the same time. The people you lead may come from more traditional roles, and helping them make the same shift is part of the job. You will also own the budget, vendor relationships, and contracts behind this work, AI tooling included.

How You'll Work
AI runs through your entire workflow, from discovery and specs to the build, tests, documentation, and reporting. We are looking for someone already working this way who can show what it has produced, not someone with a thesis on where AI is going.
Requirements here usually arrive as a conversation rather than a ticket, and you will often be the one having it. You will build inside a framework someone else runs, which means understanding a rule's reasoning before deciding it is in your way. You will be measured on whether what ships is correct and whether the business got what it actually needed, not on volume.

A typical week may include:
- Sitting with district staff, families, or the team that coordinates our transportation providers, then deciding with a Business Product Owner whether a problem belongs on the roadmap.
- Turning a conversation like that into a working prototype and using it to agree on requirements before the full build starts.
- Reviewing work with a team member who is still learning to build with agents, and explaining the reasoning behind your feedback.

Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account.

HHMI is focused on supporting and moving science forward in a variety of different ways ranging from conducting basic biomedical research, empowering educators, inspiring students, developing the next generation of scientists – even stretching into film and media production.  Our Headquarters is in the greater Washington, DC metro area and is home to over 300 employees with expertise in investments , communications, digital production, biomedical sciences, and everything in between.  The work housed here supports and augments the groundbreaking research conducted in HHMI labs across the nation.  As HHMI scientists continue to push boundaries in laboratories and classrooms, you can be sure that your contributions while working here are making a difference.

This is a role for someone who can run a function that cannot fail while rebuilding it at the same time.

HHMI is a nonprofit scientific research organization that supports scientists and educators across the country. Finance and People & Culture run the processes that pay, hire, reimburse, and support all of them. Most of those legacy processes were built for a world before Workday was mature and before AI could do real work. That world is gone. HHMI is moving procurement and expense onto Workday and is putting AI tools in the hands of every employee through EverydayAI. The open question is what the processes themselves should look like, and that is what this role answers.

HHMI’s EverydayAI initiative is putting AI tools and agents into operations across the institute. You will not need to build the business case for AI or convince leadership it matters. That work is done. What you will do is decide where AI belongs in payroll and finance processes, partner with the EverydayAI and Technology teams to build and pilot the first agents and be honest about what works and what does not.

You start with payroll, and you own it. You lead the payroll team and are accountable for every cycle running accurately and on time across the three populations. At the same time, you take the function apart end to end and redesign it: Workday-native, with AI and agents doing the work they are good at and people doing the work that needs judgment. Then you implement it with your team. You do not need to arrive as a payroll expert. You do need to learn the operation, exercise sound judgment, and lead changes that preserve accurate, on-time pay, working with an experienced payroll manager.

Once payroll is running the new way, you carry the same method into the rest of Finance and People & Culture.

You report to the Chief Financial Officer with a dotted line to the Chief of People & Culture (Human Resources). Your ideas earn their standing by making the work better for the people who do it and for the employees they serve, not by being new.

We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.
